newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines may cut tariffs on aluminium products.
newsitem.headline: Philippines may cut tariffs on aluminium products.

text.p: A Philippine cabinet committee has recommended cutting tariffs on selected aluminium products, government documents released on Friday showed.

The documents from the National Economic Development Authority's Cabinet Committee on Tariffs and Related Matters showed the committee has recommended that tariffs on aluminium tubing for textile yarn winders, bobbins and spools be cut to 3.0 percent from the present 20 percent.

It also proposed cutting tariffs for solid y-shape aluminium profiles for zippers to 3.0 percent from 20 percent, and aluminium wire rods to 10 percent until December 1997 and further down to 3.0 percent starting in 1998.
Aluminium wire rods currently face an import duty of 20 percent.
Other products set for tariff cuts were pneumatic-controlled valves and unrecorded compact discs, both to 3.0 percent from 20 percent.
The Cabinet committee has forwarded its recommendations to President Fidel Ramos for final approval.
